besu.name: Besu
besu.summary: Start with failed-frame reporting, precompile output and inclusion, and range-filter consistency. Individual replay also needs a scope decision.

erigon.name: Erigon
erigon.summary: The development build agrees on tree lookup, default filter composition, MCOPY, historical system state including trace_callMany, and the genesis reward, several of which still differ in 3.7.0. Signed-transaction validity checks and error codes need alignment with the proposal (#24329 is open), and omitted trace_filter bounds still search history instead of the proposed latest/latest default.

nethermind.name: Nethermind
nethermind.summary: 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 fixes empty trace selections, state-only output, empty-code birth/deletion markers and stack-word quantities. 2.0.0 · bec830cd still differs. Complete validation errors, tree lookup and other serialization details remain review areas.

reth.name: Reth
reth.summary: The Reth 2.5.2 nightly · 863f7055, with revm-inspectors 0.44.0, fixes tree-path lookup, default filter intersection, missing-replay nulls, replay transaction hashes, the genesis reward, omitted filter bounds, the omitted trace_callMany block, new-account stateDiff markers, EIP-7702 code changes and executing initcode in vmTrace; all of these still differ in 2.6.0 · 73a3a008. Remaining work includes simulation fees, the rest of vmTrace, the SELFDESTRUCT payload (revm #3833) and error-code alignment.

build_notes.text: **The 2.5.2 build has newer source than 2.6.0.** The version number on the development branch has not received the release-only bump. Use the commit dates above and [revision comparison](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/compare/73a3a00862a8f14f89e30da8de001456f18cfae0...4630cc588430fcf3b2846e27100a5d10cff9f949).

geth.name: Geth draft fork
geth.summary: The experimental fork follows the adopted source-review stances; its checked cases agree on every assessed decision except the H12 raw-transaction block argument and simulation pending, which remain policy observations. It is not upstream Geth support or a consensus vote. Filtering remains a bounded scan; pruning still needs runtime coverage.

anvil.name: Anvil
anvil.summary: Foundry’s development node, captured by replaying each chain instead of through Hive. The nightly 1.8.4 · 07915e32 takes up revm-inspectors 0.44.0 (#17073), which brings the EIP-7702 stateDiff, executing-bytecode and vmTrace step fixes already in Reth’s nightly, and corrects the empty trace-type selection, omitted filter bounds and the trace_callMany default block (#17078); 1.8.3 still differs on all of these. With 0.44.0 the nightly also loses the creation markers of a contract created in trace_call. Its own RPC layer still differs in tree-path lookup, missing-item results (#17089 is merged but not yet in a nightly), replay transaction hashes, conflicting data/input and zero-fee BASEFEE. Mined-trace methods also return precompile frames that its trace_call omits. The mined-probes chain cannot be replayed because Anvil cannot set a parent beacon root.

besu.observed: Individual transaction replay is unavailable.
besu.change: Add `trace_replayTransaction`; the draft requires all nine methods.

besu.observed: A recipient-only filter returns 1 of the 2 expected calls. Every recognized `mode` value is rejected with `-32602`, including `intersection` and `union`.
besu.change: Make a one-sided query select every call matching the populated list. Accept `intersection` as the default and `union` as an explicit option; reject only unknown values.

erigon.observed: Both lists are combined with OR by default (6 records instead of 1). With `mode: "intersection"`, a one-sided filter returns `[]` instead of treating the empty side as unrestricted. The unrecognized `mode: "garbage"` is accepted and treated as union.
erigon.change: Make intersection the default. Under either mode, ignore an omitted, null or empty side. Reject unknown mode values with `-32602`.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 combines both lists with OR by default (6 records instead of 1). 2.5.2 · 4630cc58 uses intersection; one-sided and explicit-mode queries agree.
reth.change: Ship the default-intersection behavior already present in 4630cc58, retaining explicit union.

nethermind.observed: `mode: "union"` returns the intersection (1 record instead of 6) and `mode: "garbage"` is accepted: the filter type has no `mode` field, so every request is intersected.
nethermind.change: Add a validated `mode` field: accept `intersection` (the default) and `union`, and reject other values with `-32602`.

besu.observed: Treats `[]` as unrestricted. Its only H04-tagged failure, on `a/filter-from-empty-to-set`, is the SELFDESTRUCT-beneficiary record it misses under every filter (H23).
besu.change: No empty-list change; match SELFDESTRUCT by beneficiary (H23).

nethermind.observed: Empty address lists match nothing (no records in any of the three `[]` cases, both builds), while omitted and null lists are unrestricted. Nethermind is the only client that reads `[]` this way, and its own eth_getLogs treats an empty address set as any address.
nethermind.change: Treat `[]` as unrestricted, like an omitted or null list and like its eth_getLogs. Open #13857 implements this in a second commit.

reth.observed: Treats `[]` as unrestricted in both builds and rejects only a null address list, because Alloy’s `TraceFilter` defaults the lists only when they are absent. Alloy #4257 fixes this and is merged but not yet released.
reth.change: Take up Alloy #4257 so a null list is treated as omitted.

besu.observed: PoS blocks include a synthetic PoW reward record.
besu.change: Remove the placeholder reward. This also changes which records pagination counts.

nethermind.observed: PoS blocks include a synthetic PoW reward record. From source, genesis replay fails because the genesis parent lookup fails; #13783 fixes `trace_block(0)` and open #13801 fixes `trace_replayBlockTransactions(0)`.
nethermind.change: Remove the placeholder reward and exclude it from pagination. Return `[]` for the genesis block from block replay too.

reth.observed: From source: on a PoW-genesis chain, `trace_block(0)` and a filter from block 0 include a block reward for the genesis coinbase.
reth.change: Emit no records for the genesis block.

besu.observed: Unknown transactions can return [] and an unknown selected block returns null.
besu.change: Return `null` for an unknown transaction, so callers can distinguish absence from a transaction with no call records. Filter bounds beyond the head already return `-32602` as proposed.

erigon.observed: A missing transaction, path or replay returns null as proposed. An unknown selected block, including a block replay, returns -32000, which the rule accepts (-32001 is recommended), and a filter bound beyond the head returns [] (an explicit "waiting for spec" choice).
erigon.change: Prefer `-32001` for an unknown selected block. Return `-32602` for a filter bound beyond the head or a reversed range.

nethermind.observed: Missing transactions or paths can produce exceptions/RPC errors, and a filter bound beyond the head returns -32000.
nethermind.change: Return `null` for an absent transaction or path, while preserving distinct unavailable-history errors. Return `-32602` for a filter bound beyond the head or a reversed range.

reth.observed: Missing individual replays error in 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 and return null in the 2.5.2 nightly · 863f7055. Both return null from trace_replayBlockTransactions for an unknown block, and -32001 for a filter bound beyond the head. See the linked pruning cases for unavailable-history classification.
reth.change: Return `null` for absent transactions and an error for an unknown selected block, including a block replay (-32001 recommended), as trace_block already does. For known transactions whose state is unavailable, use the proposed history-unavailable error (`4444`) rather than an internal error. Return `-32602` for a filter bound beyond the head.

geth.observed: The fork follows the draft on every checked H06 case, including -32602 for a filter bound beyond the head.

anvil.observed: trace_transaction and trace_block return `[]` for a missing transaction or block, a missing replay returns -32001 `transaction not found`, and trace_call at a block beyond the head returns -32602. trace_replayBlockTransactions of an unknown block returns `[]`, and a filter ending one block past the head returns the head’s records instead of an error.
anvil.change: Return `null` for a missing transaction or path and -32001 for an unknown selected block, including the trace_call and block-replay blocks, and -32602 for a filter bound beyond the head. #17089, merged after the nightly was built, returns `null` from trace_transaction.

besu.observed: Failed frames lose result information; a failed root precompile can also lack an error.
besu.change: Keep the error on the failing frame, including a failed root precompile. Add `result: {gasUsed, output}` to REVERT frames; exceptional halts may keep omitting `result`. Use the listed labels, e.g. "Mutable Call In Static Context" and "Built-in failed". `revertReason` is outside the format and may stay as an extension once `result` is present.

nethermind.observed: Failed frames omit their result.
nethermind.change: Add `result: {gasUsed, output}` to REVERT frames; exceptional halts may keep omitting `result`. Use the listed labels rather than "Static call violation" or "Error".

erigon.observed: A reverted CREATE reports `{address, code, gasUsed}` with the would-be address; exceptional halts use Go error text such as "out of gas: write protection", and a failed precheck is labelled "insufficient balance for transfer".
erigon.change: Report a reverted CREATE as `{gasUsed, output}` without address or code, and use the listed failure labels.

reth.observed: A reverted CREATE reports `{address, code, gasUsed}` with the would-be address; other failures fall back to Rust `Debug` names such as `NotActivated`.
reth.change: Report a reverted CREATE as `{gasUsed, output}` without address or code, and use the listed failure labels.

geth.observed: The fork uses the draft labels, including “Out of gas” for code above the EIP-170 limit or a failed code deposit and “Invalid code” for an EIP-3541 0xEF prefix (since e26833e3), and emits no `revertReason`.

besu.observed: A successful creation reports deployed bytecode under `output`, and `creationMethod` is missing from most create frames and computed per transaction.
besu.change: Use `code` for deployed bytecode, alongside `address` and `gasUsed`. Emit `creationMethod` on every create action, from that frame’s own opcode.

besu.observed: The zero-fee call with an empty trace selection is rejected.
besu.change: Recheck after the unsigned-call fee change (H15). This case alone does not establish a separate empty-selection bug.

erigon.observed: Empty-selection requests include rejected calls; the zero-fee case also fails the fee rule.
erigon.change: Accept an empty selection and return the execution envelope. Recheck alongside H15 before treating every rejection as a separate selection bug.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd fails empty trace selections; 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 executes them.
nethermind.change: Execute the call and return its output with the unrequested components empty/null.

besu.observed: Marker probes execute wrong-chain and ordinary-code-sender transactions. Nonce, funds, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures instead return empty success-shaped traces; these do not prove execution.
besu.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and report validation errors with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

erigon.observed: Marker probes execute nonce mismatches, both insufficient-funds cases and ordinary-code-sender transactions. CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Chain, intrinsic-gas and base-fee failures are rejected with -32000. Review feedback supports stricter validation.
erigon.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and report validation errors with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

nethermind.observed: Marker probes execute nonce mismatches and ordinary-code-sender transactions; CREATE uses the state-nonce address. Other invalid probes produce malformed JSON, which does not establish skipped validation.
nethermind.change: Apply selected-state execution validity before running signed transactions. Distinguish validation rejection from execution failure, and report validation errors with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

reth.observed: All invalid probes in the validation corpus are rejected, using -32000 or -32003. Valid EOA/delegated controls execute, and valid execution-OOG returns a trace halt.
reth.change: Retain execution validation and report rejections with the eth_sendRawTransaction error-group codes (1, 2, 800, 804, 806, 809), falling back to -32003.

besu.observed: Paired eth_call executes explicit zero fees with BASEFEE 0, while trace_call returns an internal error. An omitted fee is priced and charged at the base fee in trace_call but free in eth_call, and a supplied nonce that differs from the state nonce is rejected. Valid priced calls show the expected upfront debit in both methods; invalid trace fee/funding requests still produce generic internal errors.
besu.change: Match eth_call: default omitted fees to zero, zero BASEFEE for a zero effective price and ignore a supplied nonce. Retain priced accounting and return the eth_simulateV1 validation codes.

erigon.observed: eth_call uses BASEFEE 0 for explicit zero fees and debits priced gas upfront. trace_call rejects legacy zero, reprices typed zero and omitted fees to B, changes GASLIMIT and skips the sender gas debit; its stateDiff still credits tips. Both methods reject positive legacy/typed caps below B.
erigon.change: Match eth_call: default omitted fees to zero and run a zero effective price with BASEFEE zero. Preserve other block fields; enforce positive-price funding and simulate sender debit, refunds and beneficiary tips consistently.

nethermind.observed: Both tested builds use BASEFEE 0 in zero-fee eth_call but preserve B in trace_call, for explicit and omitted fees alike. Priced upfront debit matches in both methods when execution output is returned. 641592d2 fixes the release’s selection/output bugs. 2.0.0 truncates fee/funding rejections in trace_call; 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba includes #13666 and returns them complete but with -32000 instead of the eth_simulateV1 codes (see the [streaming investigation](../../docs/nethermind-streamed-errors.md)). An explicit zero `maxFeePerBlobGas` is rejected, and a blob fee defaulted with blob hashes present returns -32603.
nethermind.change: Zero BASEFEE whenever the effective price is zero, including omitted fees, and return validation errors with the eth_simulateV1 codes; run a zero or defaulted blob fee with BLOBBASEFEE 0; retain normal priced accounting.

reth.observed: Both methods use BASEFEE 0 for explicit zero fees and both omit priced upfront gas payment: the shared call environment sets `disable_fee_charge`, added for OP operator fees (#18634, reverted in #18645, re-added in #19073), which also skips the funding check. Both accept underpriced legacy calls and reject underpriced typed caps; a tip-only request is priced at the base fee. Method consistency agrees in 200 defined-policy pairs per build; two underfunded-value families have unclassified EVM failures. Independent priced accounting/funding checks still differ.
reth.change: Keep zero-fee compatibility. Default an omitted fee cap to zero, so a zero tip-only request runs free and a positive one is rejected as tip above cap. Reject positive legacy prices below base fee, enforce funding and simulate payment/refunds/tips during execution and later calls. Agreement with eth_call is assessed separately from this accounting requirement. Whether the L1 effect of `disable_fee_charge` is intended is an open question to Reth; complying also changes its eth_call. Asked in [reth#27476](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/27476) whether skipping fee charging and funding checks on L1 is intended.

geth.observed: The fork follows eth_call: a zero effective price, explicit or defaulted, runs with BASEFEE 0 and no fee effects, and priced calls are validated and charged. It is not an upstream consensus vote.

anvil.observed: An explicit zero fee keeps the block base fee visible as BASEFEE instead of 0. Priced calls settle the sender debit and coinbase tip in stateDiff, matching the proposal where the native clients do not.
anvil.change: Run a zero effective price with GASPRICE and BASEFEE 0 and no gas-fee balance effects; keep the priced settlement.

besu.observed: The `MCOPY` step omits its memory write, and CALL-family `mem` can copy the calling frame’s final RETURN. A value CALL’s `cost` includes the stipend and a precompile CALL’s the precompile cost; a CALL or CREATE that fails its precheck reports its net cost and a `sub`; a halted operation keeps a bogus `ex`.
besu.change: Include the bytes written at offset 32 in the MCOPY step’s memory delta, and stop copying the caller’s final RETURN into CALL-family `mem` (the copied bytes then conform). Exclude the stipend from value-CALL `cost`, include forwarded gas in precompile-call and failed-precheck `cost`, give a failed-precheck operation `sub: null`, and report a halted operation with `ex: null`.

erigon.observed: 3.8.0-dev · 3904de43 reports MCOPY and MLOAD memory and the full CALL output window, and gives SELFDESTRUCT and failed-precheck calls `sub: null` (#24291). It keeps `ex` and `store` on an operation halted by an execution error, adds a synthetic STOP at the end of code and keeps undefined opcodes with cost 0.
erigon.change: Report an operation halted by an execution error with `ex: null` and no `store`, drop the synthetic STOP and omit undefined opcodes.

nethermind.observed: CALL steps have no `mem` in both builds, a 7400 `cost` is rewritten to 9700 (the "Parity stipend" adjustment), halted operations are deleted, and a CREATE that fails its precheck reports cost 32002 without the forwarded gas. 2.0.0 · bec830cd also omits the forwarded gas from every CREATE `cost`, pushes n words for DUPn and reports `store` only when stateDiff is also selected; 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba includes #13779, #13781 and #13782.
nethermind.change: Report CALL-family `mem` (the output window or the copied bytes), remove the 7400→9700 rewrite, keep halted operations with `ex: null`, and include forwarded gas in the cost of a CREATE that fails its precheck; ship the fixes already in 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba.

geth.observed: The fork follows the step rules on every checked case; a static-context SSTORE that halts reports cost 0, which the implementation-defined halted-operation cost allows.

reth.observed: Reth 2.6.0 locks revm-inspectors 0.43.0, which reports whole-memory `mem`, pre-operation `used`, never sets `store`, and adds a synthetic STOP. The nightly takes up 0.44.0, which fixes `used` and `store` and reports the bytes a CALL copied, which the rule accepts, but reports no MLOAD memory, adds the synthetic STOP, gives precompile and empty-code callees a null `sub` and a failed-precheck call a `sub`, and keeps undefined opcodes.
reth.change: Report MLOAD memory (#504 left it out), drop the synthetic STOP, give precompile and empty-code callees `{code: "0x", ops: []}` and a failed-precheck call `sub: null`, and omit undefined opcodes; 2.6.0 also needs the 0.44.0 fixes for `used` and `store` (#504, #528).

anvil.observed: 1.8.3 locks revm-inspectors 0.43.0 (whole-memory `mem`, pre-operation `used`, no `store`). The nightly 07915e32 takes up 0.44.0 and agrees with Reth’s nightly: no MLOAD memory, a synthetic STOP after the last instruction, and a `sub` on a call that fails its precheck.
anvil.change: The revm-inspectors changes listed for Reth; 1.8.3 also needs the 0.44.0 bump (#17073) in a release.

besu.observed: The identity precompile returns bytes in the execution envelope but not its call frame.
besu.change: Copy the precompile’s return bytes into the call-frame result as well.

besu.observed: CREATE and SELFDESTRUCT address queries disagree with the corresponding block trace.
besu.change: Match creation by creator/created address, SELFDESTRUCT by executing account/beneficiary, and rewards by `author` on the recipient side.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd never matches rewards by `toAddress`; 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba includes #13800 and matches all eight rewards by author. A failed CREATE matches its attempted address through the internal `action.To`, although its record shows no address, the same policy difference Erigon and Alloy (Reth) show through the failed result address.
nethermind.change: Ship reward matching by `author` (#13800). Give a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Erigon and Alloy, while keeping sender-only matching and empty recipient filters unchanged.

erigon.observed: A failed CREATE matches its attempted address through the failed result address, the same policy difference Nethermind (`action.To`) and Alloy (Reth) show. From source, rewards are emitted for a coinbase in `toAddress` only in blocks the address indexes select: to-only and union filters return them, while intersection mode intersects the from and to txNum bitmaps, so `rewards-intersection` returns `[]` on both builds.
erigon.change: Give a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Nethermind and Alloy, while keeping sender-only matching and empty recipient filters unchanged.

reth.observed: A failed CREATE matches its attempted address through Alloy’s failed result address, the same policy difference Erigon and Nethermind show. A post-Cancun SELFDESTRUCT to self has no executing account or beneficiary, so address filters miss it: revm skips the inspector callback (revm #3834).
reth.change: Give a failed CREATE no recipient match, the H23 adoption shared with Erigon and Nethermind. The SELFDESTRUCT payload follows from revm #3833 once it reaches revm-inspectors and Reth.

besu.observed: A handled child failure can mark a successful parent or sibling as failed.
besu.change: Track errors per frame; a caught failure must not change the outcome of another frame.

besu.observed: A range filter differs from concatenating the same blocks’ traces across a fork boundary.
besu.change: Trace each block from its parent’s post-block state with its own pre-block system calls, under its own fork rules, so range filtering agrees with per-block tracing. Swapping the protocol spec alone leaves rewards, withdrawals and system calls between blocks unapplied.

besu.observed: Nested precompile frames are omitted even when their value is nonzero. A CALL that fails its balance precheck has no frame, and a CREATE that fails it leaves a successful-looking frame at `[0]`, moves the real creation below it and reports the root as using no gas.
besu.change: Retain nested precompile frames with transferred or inherited nonzero value (#11360). Continue omitting zero-value nested frames and retaining root frames. Give a CALL or CREATE that fails its balance or depth precheck a failed frame with error "Insufficient balance for transfer", no result and no children, as Besu's callTracer already records it; no submitted fix covers this.

nethermind.observed: A CALL or CREATE that fails its balance precheck has no frame, and a CREATE2 address collision has no frame either. Its callTracer also omits the precheck failure.
nethermind.change: Emit a failed frame with error "Insufficient balance for transfer", no result and no subtraces for a precheck failure, and a failed create frame with error "Contract address collision" for a collision, in trace_* and in the callTracer.

geth.observed: The fork emits a failed frame with its action and error label, no result and no subtraces for a CALL or CREATE that fails its precheck, as the revised rule requires.

anvil.observed: trace_transaction, trace_block and trace_filter return the calltree’s nested zero-value identity call as a frame, shifting its siblings; trace_call and the replays omit it. Mined traces are built from the frames recorded at mining time without the active precompile set.
anvil.change: Build mined traces with the same precompile filter as simulations: omit nested zero-value precompile frames and number the emitted tree.

erigon.observed: Root and nested `trace_get` requests fail or select the wrong record.
erigon.change: Interpret the selector as one `traceAddress` path: `[]` selects the root, `[0]` its first child.

nethermind.observed: `trace_get` returns a list and treats positions differently from a nested path; `[]` returns `[]`.
nethermind.change: Return one object for one `traceAddress` path. `[]` selects the root; a missing path returns `null`. This changes the response type.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 uses a flat selector; 2.5.2 · 4630cc58 selects the requested tree path and matches these cases.
reth.change: Ship the tree-path lookup already present in 4630cc58 (#27366). Existing flat-index callers need a migration path.

anvil.observed: `trace_get` indexes the flattened frame list and needs exactly one index: `[]` and nested paths return null, and `[1]` returns the second frame in list order.
anvil.change: Interpret the selector as one `traceAddress` path: `[]` selects the root, `[0]` its first child.

erigon.observed: No envelope deviation; output differs only through the H15 GASLIMIT environment.
erigon.change: None for the envelope; its trace_call reports GASLIMIT 2^256−1, an H15 environment difference.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd loses nonempty execution output with stateDiff-only selections; 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba retains it.
nethermind.change: Always retain output bytes. The return-42 fixture should still return its 32-byte word when only state differences are requested.

anvil.observed: 1.8.3 treats an empty trace-type list in trace_call as `["trace"]`, so it returns call frames that were not requested. The nightly 07915e32 includes #17078 and returns `trace: []` with the execution output.

erigon.observed: Malformed raw transactions and an unknown option use error codes other than `-32602`, and an unknown filter field is accepted. 3.7.0 drops `input` and every post-Berlin call field, so an `input`-only call runs with empty calldata. 3.8.0-dev · 3904de43 includes #24290, #24294, #24334 and #24351: it decodes `input` and the post-Berlin fields, treats an explicit null as omitted and rejects a chainId for another chain, but still runs `input` when `data` and `input` disagree.
erigon.change: Use JSON-RPC invalid params (`-32602`) for malformed input, unknown filter fields and disagreeing `data` and `input`, separately from execution rejection. Ship the call-field fixes in a release.

nethermind.observed: Malformed raw input, negative filter count and integer paths expose validation differences across the captured builds. An unpriced call with a null `blobVersionedHashes` or `authorizationList` takes that member’s transaction type: 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba rejects it with -32000 (“need at least 1 blob”, “EIP-7702 transaction cannot be used to create contract”) and 2.0.0 truncates the authorizationList response.
nethermind.change: Return invalid params (`-32602`) for malformed encoding. Treat a null member as omitted, so it selects no transaction type.

besu.observed: Wrong address-list types and negative count can return results rather than invalid params.
besu.change: Validate filter types and bounds and return -32602 for invalid request shapes.

reth.observed: An integer trace_get path returns null instead of invalid params. trace_filter rejects a null `mode`, `fromAddress` or `toAddress`: Alloy's `TraceFilter` defaults them only when absent. The 2026-09-26 `filter-null-fromBlock` failure came from its `"latest"` toBlock (H32), not the null; the case now names the head by number.
reth.change: Reject integer path entries with -32602; callers must convert output path integers to hex quantities. Treat a null filter member as omitted.

anvil.observed: When `data` and `input` are both set and differ, trace_call runs `input` instead of rejecting the request.

geth.observed: The fork reports a state-dependent rejection without a listed code, such as a blob fee cap below the blob base fee or a transaction type not active at the fork, as -32003 (since e26833e3), and keeps -32602 for call objects that are invalid regardless of state.

erigon.observed: A historical beacon-root lookup includes a following block’s system update.
erigon.change: Read the selected block’s post-state, before applying the next block’s system operations. Read the first trace_callMany item at the same state as trace_call (txIndex −1). Both are fixed on main (#24056, #24293); 3.7.0 carries only the trace_call fix.

besu.observed: From source: block replay does not run the block’s pre-block system calls, so a transaction that reads the EIP-4788 or EIP-2935 contracts sees stale storage. The captured H28 probes use trace_call only.
besu.change: Apply the block’s pre-execution system calls before replaying its transactions ([Besu #10953](https://github.com/besu-eth/besu/pull/10953)).

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd uses padded byte strings for VM stack words. 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 includes PR #13750 and emits minimal stack quantities; both builds still encode storage operands as a padded key and non-minimal values such as 0x00.
nethermind.change: Ship the minimal-quantity stack encoding verified in 641592d2, e.g. 0x2a rather than a 32-byte padded string, and apply it to vmTrace store keys and values.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd can leave truncated JSON on the wire when a streamed trace is rejected, including a null authorizationList on an unpriced call and a defaulted blob fee. 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba includes #13666 and returns one complete error response.
nethermind.change: Ship #13666 in a release.

besu.observed: The initial zero-fee callMany result contains a complete JSON-RPC error envelope nested inside result.
besu.change: Return a top-level error when execution is rejected; never serialize an error envelope as a successful result.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd reports a pre-Cancun deletion as `*` to `null` for balance, nonce and code. 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 includes PR #13668 and restores the deletion markers, while retaining existing accounts after Cancun. From source, a deleted account lists its written slots as `*` to zero.
nethermind.change: Ship the account-deletion serializer fix verified in 641592d2, retain the pre/post-Cancun regression cases, and report a deleted account’s storage as `{}`.

reth.observed: Pre-Cancun account deletion loses code/nonce deletion markers. After Cancun, a SELFDESTRUCT to self reports a zero executing account and balance because revm skips the inspector callback when the opcode changes no state (revm #3834).
reth.change: Report the removed code and nonce before Cancun; preserve existing accounts after EIP-6780. Fixed by revm-inspectors #510, released in 0.44.0 and taken up by the nightly; 0.44.0 lists accessed nonzero slots as `-`, which open revm-inspectors #530 changes to `storage: {}`. The SELFDESTRUCT payload is fixed by open revm #3833, which then needs revm-inspectors and Reth uptake.

geth.observed: A deleted account lists its written slots with `-`.
geth.change: Report a deleted account’s storage as `{}`.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 omits transactionHash in individual replays; 2.5.2 · 4630cc58 includes it.
reth.change: Ship the replay metadata fix already present in 4630cc58.

anvil.change: Include `transactionHash` in trace_replayTransaction results, as block replays do.

reth.observed: EIP-7702 delegation code changes are missing from `stateDiff`.
reth.change: Include net authorization code set, replacement and clearing, even for existing accounts and when the subsequent execution reverts. Fixed by revm-inspectors #509, released in revm-inspectors 0.44.0 and taken up by the Reth nightly (df7b7fdf); 2.6.0 still differs until a Reth release carries it.

reth.observed: Creation `vmTrace.code` does not contain the expected executing initcode.
reth.change: Attach the creation frame’s initcode to its VM trace, including in block replay. Fixed by revm-inspectors #511, released in revm-inspectors 0.44.0 and taken up by the Reth nightly (df7b7fdf); 2.6.0 still differs until a Reth release carries it.

erigon.observed: Omitting both bounds starts at block 1 rather than head 48, and supplying only toBlock 2 searches the early range, unlike Erigon’s own eth_getLogs. The default `--rpc.blockrange.limit` of 1000 already rejects an omitted fromBlock on any chain above block 1000.
erigon.change: Default an omitted fromBlock to latest and return `-32602` when an explicit end precedes that implicit start. Record it as a breaking change: only archive operators who set the range limit to 0 lose results, silently, and they migrate by sending `fromBlock: "earliest"`.

reth.observed: 2.6.0 · 73a3a008 starts at block 1 when both bounds are omitted, and toBlock 2 alone searches the early range. the 2.5.2 nightly includes #27411 (since df7b7fdf): both bounds default to latest and toBlock 2 alone returns -32602.
reth.change: Ship #27411 in a release, preserving explicit historical bounds and resource-limit errors.

geth.observed: The fork defaults omitted bounds to latest and returns -32602 when toBlock precedes the implicit start.
geth.change: No change. This is draft-fork work, not a finding about upstream Geth trace support.

nethermind.observed: Both builds already default omitted bounds to latest; an explicit toBlock before the implicit latest start returns -32000.
nethermind.change: Return `-32602` for the reversed range.

anvil.observed: 1.8.3 starts an omitted fromBlock at block 0 and an omitted toBlock at the head, so toBlock 2 alone searches the early range. The nightly 07915e32 includes #17078: omitted bounds default to latest and toBlock 2 alone is rejected as a reversed range. Ranges are capped at 300 blocks.

besu.observed: trace_callMany with one argument returns -32602 Invalid number of params; explicit latest returns NUMBER 48.
besu.change: Accept an omitted block argument and execute against latest.

reth.observed: An omitted trace_callMany block returns NUMBER 49 on both tested builds, while explicit latest and trace_call defaults return 48. Main already defaults to latest (#27410).
reth.change: Ship the latest default from main; retain pending only when explicitly requested and supported.

anvil.observed: 1.8.3 runs an omitted trace_callMany block at pending (NUMBER 49), while trace_call defaults to latest. The nightly 07915e32 includes #17078 and defaults to latest.

besu.observed: trace_filter with safe or pending bounds returns -32603 Internal error; earliest succeeds. Pending call simulations run on the head block (NUMBER 48), and `trace_block` and `trace_replayBlockTransactions` at pending trace head block 48, indistinguishable from latest.
besu.change: Resolve safe/finalized tags when available. Reject pending filter bounds with `-32602`. For `trace_block`, `trace_replayBlockTransactions`, `trace_call` and `trace_callMany`, evaluate pending in a real pending environment or reject it with `-32602`, rather than an internal error or latest; accept a block hash for `trace_call` and `trace_callMany`.

reth.observed: trace_filter rejects earliest, safe and pending with -32602, although numeric bounds work: Alloy’s `TraceFilter` types the bounds as quantities, so even "latest" is rejected. Explicit pending call simulations return NUMBER 49, and `trace_block` traces a locally built pending block under its non-canonical hash; on the frozen chain, with no pending transactions, `trace_block` and `trace_replayBlockTransactions` at pending return `[]`.
reth.change: Accept latest, earliest, safe and finalized filter bounds (an Alloy `TraceFilter` change), with earliest as the lowest available block, and keep rejecting pending bounds with `-32602`. Pending block traces are allowed; how their records are localized is still open.

erigon.observed: 3.7.0 · bdc78cc4 rejects pending with -32000 (“tracing on top of pending is not supported”). 3.8.0-dev · 3904de43 includes #24345 and rejects pending in every trace method with -32602. Both builds accept a block hash as a trace_filter bound, as a string or an EIP-1898 object.
erigon.change: Ship #24345 in a release. Reject block-hash filter bounds with `-32602`, as eth_getLogs range bounds do.

geth.observed: `earliest` resolves to block 0 rather than the lowest available block. `trace_block` and `trace_replayBlockTransactions` at pending trace the miner’s pending block, which is empty on the frozen chain, so the capture cannot show its environment.
geth.change: Resolve `earliest` to the lowest available block, as eth_getLogs does, and keep 4444 for explicit numbers below retained history.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd resolves a pending filter bound to the latest block, as Parity’s fallback did, runs pending call simulations on the head block (NUMBER 48), and traces the head block for `trace_block` and `trace_replayBlockTransactions` at pending: Nethermind builds no pending block for RPC (`BlockTree.PendingHash` returns the head). 2.1.0-preview · 5ece5fba includes #13936 and rejects pending in every trace method with -32602. Both builds accept a block hash as a trace_filter bound, as a string or an EIP-1898 object.
nethermind.change: Ship #13936 in a release. Reject block-hash filter bounds with `-32602`, as eth_getLogs range bounds do.

nethermind.observed: 2.0.0 · bec830cd omits the empty-code birth marker for transfers, empty-runtime CREATE and fresh fee recipients. 2.1.0-unstable · 641592d2 contains PR #13668 and fixes these cases in the fresh Fedora capture; existing-account markers remain unchanged.
nethermind.change: Ship the account-existence serialization fix verified in 641592d2. The [H17 audit](../../docs/h17-assessment-audit.md) retains the source explanation and before/after evidence.

reth.observed: A first transfer to an absent account reports balance as a change from zero and code/nonce as unchanged. revm-inspectors reserves added fields for contract creation. Simple contract-creation markers are correct, including when H15 environment bytes differ; see the [H17 audit](../../docs/h17-assessment-audit.md).
reth.change: Adopt [revm-inspectors #526](https://github.com/paradigmxyz/revm-inspectors/pull/526), released in revm-inspectors 0.44.0 and taken up by the Reth nightly (df7b7fdf); 2.6.0 still differs until a Reth release carries it. The [H17 audit](../../docs/h17-assessment-audit.md) retains the Fedora regression results.

geth.observed: Zero-to-value and value-to-zero slots on an account that exists at both endpoints are reported with `+` and `-`.
geth.change: Use `*` with 32-byte from/to words for every slot change on a surviving account; reserve `+` and `-` for account birth and deletion.

anvil.observed: A first transfer to an absent account, including the zero-address fee recipient, reports balance as a change from zero and code/nonce as unchanged. 1.8.3 marks a contract created in trace_call with `+`; the nightly 07915e32, on revm-inspectors 0.44.0, reports it as `*` changes with balance `=`, although Reth’s nightly on the same release marks it correctly.
anvil.change: Mark every field of an account absent before the call with `+`, for transfers and creations alike; check how Anvil’s state database reports a missing account to the 0.44.0 state-diff builder.

besu.observed: `trace_callMany` does not start each call at a transaction boundary, so a later call’s SSTORE uses the pre-bundle original value: the second `initial/call-many-priced` call uses 5,600 gas less than on every other build.
besu.change: Mark a transaction boundary before each call, as block replay already does, so original values, access sets, transient storage and refunds start afresh.
